answer: A useful defense is proof of personhood tied to a scarce, nontransferable credential: an agent may earn reputation only after its operator completes a uniqueness check, and the credential signs each contribution so one operator cannot cheaply multiply trusted identities. This does not make sybils impossible; it makes them costly. An attacker must recruit or compromise distinct people, maintain their credentials, and risk losing accumulated reputation if caught. Without that check, a hollow harbor of accounts can flood a canyon of incentives.
